title: Clinton Presidential Library: Records Concerning Prediction Markets, Event Contracts, and Related Futures/Gambling Regulation (Jan. 20, 1993 to Jan. 20, 2001)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I request copies of the following Clinton Presidential Records and Vice-Presidential Records created or received between January 20, 1993, and January 20, 2001:

1. Direct references to prediction markets. Records mentioning the Iowa Electronic Markets or Iowa Political Stock Market, the Foresight Exchange ("idea futures"), the Hollywood Stock Exchange, or any similar online or academic market trading contracts on elections, policy outcomes or events. Include correspondence with, or about, their operators or sponsors.

2. Commodity futures regulation as it touched event or political contracts. Memoranda, briefing papers, correspondence and email concerning (a) CFTC staff no-action relief for event-based or political contracts, or (b) whether such contracts fall under the Commodity Exchange Act. Include related material generated in connection with CFTC reauthorization, the 1998 OTC derivatives concept release, the Commodity Futures Modernization Act, and the President's Working Group on Financial Markets, to the extent it addresses event, political or "information" markets.

3. Gambling law. Policy memoranda, legal analyses and correspondence addressing the distinction between internet gambling and event-based futures contracts, including analyses of the Wire Act (18 U.S.C. § 1084), the Internet Gambling Prohibition Act, and the National Gambling Impact Study Commission.

Offices to search (as applicable): National Economic Council; Council of Economic Advisers; Domestic Policy Council; Office of the Counsel to the President; Office of Science and Technology Policy; Office of Legislative Affairs; Office of the Vice President. Please include WHORM subject files and the White House email system (ARMS) records for these offices.

Search terms for your use: prediction market(s); idea futures; political futures; event contract(s); election futures; information market(s); Iowa Electronic Markets; Iowa Political Stock Market; Foresight Exchange; Hollywood Stock Exchange; CFTC no-action; Wire Act; internet gambling; ideosphere.com; iem.biz.uiowa.edu, and biz.uiowa.edu/iem. 

Please note: the specific ideosphere.com; iem.biz.uiowa.edu, and biz.uiowa.edu/iem URLs were all in use in the 1990s. Please include searches for these specific URLs and the longer http://www.ideosphere.com/; http://www.biz.uiowa.edu/iem; and http://www.iem.biz.uiowa.edu URLs in targeted searches. 

Request handling:

• Fees: I am a private citizen who is interested in the evolution in the development of prediction markets, and I request that fees be waived because disclosure is in the public interest. 

• Format: Electronic copies, rolling releases as processed.

• Redactions: Segregate and release all non-exempt portions, and cite the specific exemption for each withholding.

• Referrals: If records implicate another agency's equities, please consult or refer rather than deny.

• No records: If no responsive records are found, please describe the offices, series and search terms used.

• Scope: If you consider the request too broad, please call or email me to narrow it before closing it.

Thank you for the work that the Clinton Presidential Library does every day. Thank you also for the commitment to transparency.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
